headline: Planning commission approves home exemption; chair raises water capacity questions

meeting.summary: The commission approved an SMA exemption for a single-family home after the chair questioned water and wastewater capacity in the subdivision.
meeting.recap: Staff said exemptions are for projects with little or no impact on the environment.[[0:06:04]] Staff said the home is not on the shoreline and is outside the flood hazard area.[[0:06:15]] The applicant's representative said one covered area was listed wrong and is 980 square feet.[[0:07:26]] The county's lawyer called it a clerical error that does not affect the public notice.[[0:07:54]] The chair asked if water and wastewater systems can support all the building in the subdivision.[[0:10:42]] Staff said water and wastewater are reviewed at the building permit stage.[[0:11:26]] The chair said older subdivisions need new reviews of how much building their water and resources can support.[[0:14:45]] The commission voted unanimously to approve the exemption.[[0:22:20]] The department said this was the county lawyer's last meeting.[[0:24:32]] Staff said Title 19 is the county zoning code, which is being rewritten.[[0:28:02]] The next meeting is July 22 at 11:00 a.m., with a Title 19 update from the planning implementation division.[[0:29:15]]
meeting.next: Staff will ask management for an update on new commission members who were interviewed and report back in August. The department said the corporation counsel office is making sure the commission will have a lawyer at its next meeting.

moments.q: Chair asks about water and wastewater capacity

trackerIssues.title: Rewrite of Title 19 county zoning code
